narrative_purpose: Shows extinction debt at the misleading moment after habitat loss: adult specialists remain alive around the scar, but their unique breeding sites are gone and no young replace them.
subject: A burned giant-tree clearing surrounded by surviving forest, viewed across three seasonal states. Immediately after disturbance, several adult hollow-dependent birds and canopy-soil invertebrates remain alive on neighbouring branches while searching the empty scar. In the next state, the same ageing adults crowd the last unsuitable perch beside a shattered cavity section, with abandoned unhatched eggs and no canopy-soil mat. In the final state, the perch is empty and only generalist species cross the regrown scrub. The number of adult specialists declines without any mass-death scene.
scene: The edge of the Hometree burn scar rendered as a restrained ecological time study, with the same stump, branch and horizon anchoring every state.
camera: Matched wide side views compressed into one continuous panorama from recent ash to later scrub.
light: Cool indigo aftermath shifts gradually toward living teal regrowth; a sparse amber accent stays on the last surviving adult and disappears in the final state.
palette: Indigo ash and shadow, teal regrowth, cyan remnant fungi, one diminishing amber specialist accent.
style: Painterly disturbance-ecology plate focused on absence and demographic lag rather than spectacle.
detail_level: Crisp surviving adults, destroyed nesting cavity, missing canopy-soil substrate and later empty perch; background remains atmospheric.
composition: Three time states read left to right using the same central stump and perch. Keep dark space near the surviving adult, failed breeding site and final empty perch for callouts.
consistency_notes: The teaching point is delayed demographic collapse: adults survive the initial event but reproduction fails because obligate structures are missing. Do not show immediate mass mortality.
negative_prompt: no text, no arrows, no mass grave, no dramatic battle, no instant extinction, no chart, no photo or CGI look
